overall: The AG found the Millville Finance Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law on the February 27 notice complaint, and separately recommended (not ordered) that the April 3 minutes be amended for inadequate detail.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Feb 27 meeting discussed a topic not on the notice: Chair's prepared statement and a member's follow-up remarks about financial information requests.
allegations.key_passage: As such, the chair was not required to separately list the statement on the meeting notice as it was not a reasonably anticipated topic.

allegations.summary: Complainant suggested the Committee failed to notify the Board and Town Accountant that they would be discussed at the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Committee discussed the Board and Town Accountant in open session, it was not required to personally notify either of them that it would be discussing them.

allegations.summary: Not raised by the complainant; AG noted the April 3 open session minutes appear too thin to summarize the roughly three-hour discussion, and recommended amendment.
allegations.key_passage: we note that the minutes appear inadequate to meet the standard required by the Open Meeting Law

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
